name: Bean Fly (Bean Stem Maggot)
description: A small fly whose larvae tunnel into bean stems, causing wilting, stem swelling, and plant death. It is a major pest of beans and cowpea in Africa, especially during wet seasons.
symptoms: Small puncture marks on leaves from adult feeding
Mining tunnels in leaf petioles and stems
Stem swelling at the base (pith damaged)
Stunted growth and plant death in severe cases
Dark pupae visible at stem base
treatments: Apply systemic insecticides (dimethoate, imidacloprid) at seedling stage
Spray neem-based insecticides at first leaf stage
Use carbofuran granules in planting hole for early protection
prevention: Plant early to avoid peak bean fly populations
Use tolerant bean and cowpea varieties
Ensure good soil fertility for strong seedling growth
Hill up soil around seedling stems to encourage adventitious roots
Practice crop rotation with non-legume crops
